title: Bound large HTTP responses and SSE frames at the data source, so no response or frame can grow without limit
outcome: Every HTTP route and SSE producer the host serves has an explicit data bound (pagination, a bounded projection, or a hard limit) at its source. The 64 MiB encoded-output cap from w-492e stays only as a safety fuse that ordinary workloads never reach, and clients handle paged and projected data without treating it as deletion or looping on it.
acceptance: The P0 safety fuse w-492e7ae8a0fd (64 MiB encoded cap, typed refusal, history-clone fix, client terminal handling) has landed before any wave-1 item lands; it is a precursor, not a member of this epic's data-bounding work.

Wave 1, in order after w-492e: w-bf22f922e573 (transcript, history and text deltas), w-8710a74f642e (state and mutation responses), w-b6757f632670 (ResponseBoard), w-570f9f9331f8 (mailboxes, including the federation/relay aggregation). Each is completed with its own accepted criteria.

Wave 2: w-c4ccf7b1b89a (filesystem and search), w-1c7ebf109bbb (Git), w-156d9f667530 (workspace watcher batches); then the P2 items w-42506386538a (catalogs), w-bfd3875aea73 (reviews), w-d04506033449 (test and Work working sets). Each is completed with its own accepted criteria, or explicitly superseded or cancelled with a recorded reason.

After all members complete, a read-only re-census from the then-current master (the same method as w-9af00ebbaa71) finds no HTTP or SSE producer whose serialized object is unbounded by design; any remaining exception is recorded with its bound and justification.
